tagline: Joshua trees, dry lake beds and mountain ranges along a desert highway.
intro: Route 247 crosses the Mojave Desert between Barstow and Yucca Valley, using Barstow Road and Old Woman Springs Road. The two-lane Old Woman Springs section parallels the north side of the San Bernardino Mountains through Johnson Valley. Caltrans designated the Barstow-to-Yucca Valley corridor a scenic byway in 2025. Joshua trees, creosote and cholla grow along a corridor of mesas, sand washes, lava flows and mountain ranges.

Before state ownership, the corridor carried miners and freight heading for the Dale District east of Twentynine Palms, then homesteaders arriving after World War II. In 1964, the Lucerne Valley Chamber of Commerce began campaigning for a state highway along Old Woman Springs Road between Lucerne Valley and Yucca Valley. By 1969, county roads connected Barstow, Lucerne Valley and Yucca Valley. San Bernardino County transferred Barstow Road and Old Woman Springs Road to the state in 1972, while agreeing to carry out further improvements after state maintenance began.

Driving south from Barstow takes you through the Ord Mountains and past Lucerne Dry Lake toward Lucerne Valley. There, follow Old Woman Springs Road southeast through Johnson Valley and the western tip of Landers. Flamingo Heights comes before the final junction with Route 62 in Yucca Valley.
notice: Joshua trees, creosote bush, cholla and yucca are among the corridor’s desert plants.

moments.title: Ord Mountains
moments.text: The Ord Mountains run generally east to west, with Ord Mountain rising to 6,309 feet. The range is approximately 14 miles long and lies southeast of Barstow, above North Lucerne Valley. These mountains belonged to the Ord Mountain Mining District in the late nineteenth century. In the early twentieth century, miners extracted about 500 tons of gold and silver ore; copper mining followed during the World Wars. The Bureau of Land Management administers the area, and the Ord Mountain Trail passes through one section of the range.

moments.title: Lucerne Lake
moments.text: Lucerne Lake is a dry lake bed in the Mojave Desert, 15 miles east of Apple Valley. It measures approximately 3.7 miles long and 5 miles at its widest point. Small meteorites have been found here and at nearby Rabbit Springs Dry Lake.

moments.title: Landers
moments.text: Landers lies in Homestead Valley, north of Yucca Valley and Flamingo Heights. Landers grew from gold prospecting at Goat Mountain, beginning with Charles Reche in 1914. From the late 1940s through the 1970s, UFO enthusiasts gathered for conventions focused on Giant Rock and the Integratron. George Van Tassel built the Integratron between 1957 and 1977. Its wooden dome uses 16 laminated spines held together at the top by a ton of concrete. North of Landers, remains of Giant Rock’s packed-sand airstrip and a concrete cafe pad survive from Van Tassel’s activities there.
